stem: The reducing agent $\text{LiAlH}_{4}$ can be synthesised by reacting aluminium chloride with lithium hydride, $\text{LiH}$.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text:
At $200^{\circ}\text{C}$, aluminium chloride exists as $\text{Al}_{2}\text{Cl}_{6}(\text{g})$.

Draw the structure of $\text{Al}_{2}\text{Cl}_{6}(\text{g})$, showing fully any coordinate (dative covalent) bonds in the molecule.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text:
At $1000^{\circ}\text{C}$, aluminium chloride exists as $\text{AlCl}_{3}(\text{g})$.

State the bond angle in $\text{AlCl}_{3}(\text{g})$.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text:
Lithium hydride contains the ions $\text{Li}^{+}$ and $\text{H}^{-}$.

State the electronic configuration of these two ions.

parts.label: (a)(iv)
parts.text:
$\text{LiAlH}_{4}$ decomposes slowly to form $\text{LiAl}(\text{s})$ and $\text{H}_{2}(\text{g})$.

$$\text{LiAlH}_{4}(\text{s}) \rightarrow \text{LiAl}(\text{s}) + 2\text{H}_{2}(\text{g})$$

$\text{LiAl}(\text{s})$ shows metallic bonding.

Describe metallic bonding.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
$\text{LiAlH}_{4}$ cannot be used in aqueous solution because it reacts with water to produce $\text{LiOH}(\text{aq})$, $\text{H}_{2}(\text{g})$ and a white precipitate which is soluble in excess sodium hydroxide.

Identify the white precipitate.

parts.label: (c)
(c)(i)
parts.text: State the reagents and conditions required for reaction 1.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
Only one of the students successfully prepares 2-hydroxybutanoic acid.

Identify which of Q or R is 2-hydroxybutanoic acid and explain the difference between reactions 2 and 3.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text:
A third student prepares 2-hydroxybutanoic acid using propanal as the starting material. In step 1 the student reacts propanal with a mixture of $\text{NaCN}$ and $\text{HCN}$.

{{figure:pdf_visual_03.png}}

Draw the mechanism for the reaction of propanal with the mixture of $\text{NaCN}$ and $\text{HCN}$ to form **S**.

- Identify the ion that reacts with propanal.
- Draw the structure of the intermediate of the reaction.
- Include all charges, partial charges, lone pairs and curly arrows.

{{figure:pdf_visual_04.png}}

parts.label: (c)(iv)
parts.text:
Complete the equation for the reaction in step 2, when S is heated under reflux with $\text{HCl}(\text{aq})$.

$$\text{C}_{2}\text{H}_{5}\text{CH}(\text{OH})\text{CN} + \ldots\ldots \rightarrow \text{C}_{2}\text{H}_{5}\text{CH}(\text{OH})\text{COOH} + \ldots\ldots$$

parts.label: (c)(v)
parts.text:
The infrared spectrum of an organic compound is shown. The organic compound is either S or 2-hydroxybutanoic acid.

{{figure:pdf_visual_05.png}}

Deduce the identity of the compound. Give **two** reasons for your answer.

In your answer, identify any relevant absorptions **above** $1500\text{ cm}^{-1}$ in the spectrum and the bonds that correspond to these absorptions.
